text:
sre-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-12 pod:redwood-runtime-5 crashed (OOM) on cuda:0. Observed repeated CUDA OOM errors despite reported headroom. Auto-escalation -> #incidents.

anya: seeing the alert, pulling logs now. what model was this serving?

devin: this was a high-traffic dedicated job serving text-generation v2 (seq len ~1024). bucketed to gpu-node-12, ~70% nominal headroom per telemetry.

jamie: attaching last 30s of allocator logs.

jamie: ```
2026-03-15T09:07:21Z runtime: reserve: allocated 1.2G reserved-blocks
2026-03-15T09:07:22Z allocator: slab-coalesce failed: free_span_count mismatch
2026-03-15T09:07:23Z runtime: attempt alloc 2.4G -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
2026-03-15T09:07:23Z kvcache: spill triggered for prefix 0x7ff... -> success
2026-03-15T09:07:24Z runtime: headroom report: 1.8G free (reported)
2026-03-15T09:07:24Z kernel: cudaErrorUnknown during memcopy, fallback path
```

maria: nvidia-smi from node at time of crash:

maria: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.03    Driver Version: 530.41.03    CUDA Version: 12.1    |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-80GB  Off        | 00000000:3D:00.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
|  0     -    -       14321  G      /usr/bin/X                         200MiB |
|  0     -    -       20111  C      /opt/redwood/runtime                76.5GiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

ryan: reported memory 80GB total, runtime process 76.5GB. headroom should have allowed remainder for allocations. possible fragmentation or reserved-block leak.

ops-bot: @oncall-nate you have been paged for incident gpu-oom-3642001234.

oncall-nate: on it. I'll gather allocation and slab maps. please keep traffic steering active.

anya: quick mitigation — can we toggle kvcache spill threshold to force earlier eviction and free contiguous pages?

devin: yes, we can lower kvcache.max_prefix_bytes from 4G -> 1G for this node group, but risk of higher token cost. doing a rolling change to node pool-12 now.

jamie: initiating kube rollout: kubectl patch daemonset redwood-runtime -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"oom-mitigation":"2026-03-15T09:10:00Z"}}}}}'

maria: traffic steering: moved 30% of requests for the dedicated job to fallback region (eu-west-2) at 09:10:45Z. will increase to 60% if errors continue.

oncall-nate: confirmed a restart of container on gpu-node-12 after eviction. post-restart logs show allocator reclaimed 3.6G in small spans but failed to coalesce into larger contiguous block.

jamie: allocator debug dump (truncated):

jamie: ```
SLAB_MAP:
small_span: total 12G free in 128 chunks
large_span: free 2.1G in non-contiguous fragments
reserved_blocks: count 24 -> sizes [512M x 6, 256M x 10, 64M x8]
coalesce_pass: merged 64M chunks but merge threshold 256M unmet -> coalescence abort
```

devin: that matches fragmentation hypothesis — many small free spans but no contiguous 2G region for the allocator to hand out for a big activations allocation. reserved_blocks also pinned, not freeable by normal eviction because marked "pinned_for_prefetch".

anya: can we drop prefetch for this model temporarily? it pins reserved blocks during kvcache warm-up.

devin: setting model runtime flag prefetch=false on the pod template and rolling. I expect a drop in first-token latency for cold prefixes but should avoid pinning.

maria: telemetry update: error rate for the model rose to 6.2% at peak (09:09-09:11), avg latency spike +450ms for affected requests. ~14 customer sessions returned 500/503.

oncall-nate: customer impact note: three paying customers on Dedicated lost streams momentarily; engineering notified via escalation channel. CS is drafting outreach.

ryan: mitigation timeline so far:
- 09:07:23 alert fired (OOM)
- 09:08:10 kube auto-restart container -> crash loop (2x)
- 09:09:00 traffic steering engaged (30%)
- 09:10:12 kvcache threshold lowered on node pool-12
- 09:10:40 prefetch disabled for v2 model on problematic pods
- 09:11:05 container stable after restart, no new OOMs observed for 18m

ops-bot: INCIDENT severity set to SEV2. add postmortem label and link to incident board.

anya: follow-ups to include in postmortem:
- allocator coalescence heuristics review (merge thresholds)
- reserved-block lifecycle: why pinned blocks weren't reclaimable
- kvcache prefetch behavior under heavy QPS
- automated traffic fallback thresholds for Dedicated pools

devin: quick patch idea: allow evacuate_reserved_blocks() to ignore pinned_for_prefetch if memory pressure > 85% and fallback available. will prototype and QA.

maria: CS update: draft sent to affected customers at 09:40. included explanation and immediate remediation steps (we migrated traffic and applied node-level mitigations). no data exfiltration, no model correctness issues.

jamie: capturing a short snippet for the timeline in the incident tracker. also saved allocator core dump to s3://redwood-incidents/3642001234/allocator-core.tgz

ryan: monitoring for recurrence: set a watch to alert if any node in pool-12 has >3 OOMs in 1h or if contiguous free >2G falls below threshold for 5m.

oncall-nate: handing off to morning shift. I'll leave runbook notes and current mitigations in the incident ticket. If it flares back up, please page me immediately.

anya: thanks all — nice quick work. marking this thread resolved for now; keeping postmortem in progress. :white_check_mark:
